Follow the facility security policy (ies) for storage and management of this instrument. ALARA principle ALARA “as low as reasonably achievable” is the guiding principle for the use of diagnostic ultrasound. Qualified ultrasound examiners, using good judgment and insight, determine the exposure that is as low as reasonably achievable. There are no sufficient rules to determine the correct response to every situation. Therefore, it is the responsibility of the ultrasound examiner to keep exposure low, bioeffects minimal, and images diagnostic. A thorough knowledge of the imaging modes, transducer capability, System setting, and scanning technique is necessary. The imaging mode determines the nature of the ultrasound beam. Transducer capability depends upon transducer frequency, penetration, resolution, and field of view. It is the scanning technique of the qualified ultrasound examiner along with patient variability that determine the setting content throughout the exam. There are variables that affect the way the ultrasound examiner implements the ALARA principle. These variables include body size, location of the bone relative to the focal point, ultrasound attenuation in the body, and ultrasound exposure time. Exposure time is an especially useful variable because it can be controlled by the ultrasound examiner. The ability to limit the exposure over time supports the ALARA principle.
